title: Ordered branching store with lower and upper links
summary: Every written address becomes a node with a lower and an upper link. Writing descends from the root, going lower for a smaller address and upper otherwise, and attaches a new node at the first missing link; reading descends the same way. A three-mode controller decides what is written and read; the setting is found by search on a few examples.
core_idea: Keep addresses as nodes ordered by comparison and descend to read or write, under a searched three-mode controller.

state.name: Nk
state.meaning: Address of each node, in creation order; at most C nodes.

state.name: Nb
state.meaning: Item of each node, -1 when cleared.

state.name: Lo
state.meaning: Index of the lower child of each node, -1 if missing.

state.name: Up
state.meaning: Index of the upper child of each node, -1 if missing.

state.name: ctl
state.meaning: Controller state outside the store: setting (mu, sigma, H), the waiting token p, flag w, counters c, o, d and the learned symbol sets Z and A.

state.name: M
state.meaning: Learned translation from a read result to an emitted symbol, at most N entries for an alphabet of N symbols.

update.plain: one of three write disciplines picked by learning, pairing, positional or depth-indexed, drives ins and del; writing halts at the learned stop symbol and the emitted-symbol count o starts there
update.name: controller

update.latex: \mathrm{ins}(a,b):\; i \leftarrow \text{root};\; \text{while } i \ne -1: (Nk_i = a \Rightarrow Nb_i \leftarrow b;\; a < Nk_i \Rightarrow i \leftarrow Lo_i;\; \text{else } i \leftarrow Up_i);\; \text{attach a new node at the missing link}
update.plain: ins descends from the root comparing a with each node's address and either overwrites the node holding a or attaches a new node where the path ends; a write that would exceed C entries is dropped
update.name: attach

update.latex: \mathrm{del}(a,b):\; Nb_i \leftarrow -1 \text{ at the node holding } a
update.plain: del clears the item of the node holding a
update.name: clear

readout.plain: readout follows held partners from the token (at most H fetches, ending at a member of A) or reads position o or depth d, then applies the learned translation M
readout.name: readout

readout.latex: \mathrm{get}(a):\; \text{descend as in ins};\; \text{return } Nb_i \text{ at the node with } Nk_i = a,\; \varnothing \text{ if the path ends or } Nb_i = -1
readout.plain: get descends from the root by comparisons and returns the item of the node holding a

learning.description: The learner picks a setting by search: the separators Z are symbols present exactly once in every example, the answer set A is the set of targets, and each (mode, stop) candidate is run over the m examples with M fitted by majority; the most accurate candidate is used.
learning.few_shot_argument: The candidate count is about 3|Z| + 4, so m = 12 small-case examples (L, K, T at most 4, depth 2, two hops) single out the right one.

complexity.constants_notes: A descent visits at most the tree height, which is C in the worst case (addresses written in sorted order); random orders give about 2 ln C.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Search over a handful of controller settings with a majority translation.

prediction.statement: With m = 12 training examples the learned controller reaches accuracy at least 0.99 on copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, nesting at depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops, on three seeds.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: String mode with C = L copies L = 8, 32, 64 over D = 4 with per-string accuracy 1.0 within 4C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = K and H = 1 answers K = 8, 32, 64 with per-query accuracy 1.0 within 4C + N + 16 words (N = 2K + 17 at K = 64 with V = 16).
Nesting mode with C = depth predicts the legal closer at depth 2, 4, 8, 16 with accuracy 1.0 within 4C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2T and H = 2 answers f(g(x)) at T = 4, 16, 32 with accuracy 1.0 within 4C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2(hops + 1) and H = hops + 1 resolves chains of 1, 4, 8 hops with accuracy 1.0 within 4C + N + 16 words.
The search learner reaches 0.99 from m = 12 examples on seeds 0, 1, 2 for copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops.

For any fixed capacity C, recall of K = C + 1 distinct pairs over V = 16 symbols fails on some instance: the store holds at most C pairs, so one probe's item is absent and is answered from at most 16 guesses (at C = 64 this is K = 65, above every P2 size).

toy_example.description: Five addresses attached, then the depth of the deepest node and two fetches.
toy_example.python:
import json
Nk, Nb, Lo, Up = [], [], [], []
def ins(a, b):
    if not Nk:
        Nk.append(a); Nb.append(b); Lo.append(-1); Up.append(-1)
        return 0
    i, depth = 0, 0
    while True:
        if Nk[i] == a:
            Nb[i] = b
            return depth
        side = Lo if a < Nk[i] else Up
        depth += 1
        if side[i] < 0:
            Nk.append(a); Nb.append(b); Lo.append(-1); Up.append(-1)
            side[i] = len(Nk) - 1
            return depth
        i = side[i]
def get(a):
    i = 0 if Nk else -1
    while i >= 0:
        if Nk[i] == a:
            return Nb[i]
        i = Lo[i] if a < Nk[i] else Up[i]
    return -1
depths = [ins(a, b) for a, b in [(5, 30), (2, 31), (8, 32), (6, 33), (7, 34)]]
print(json.dumps({"depths": depths, "get6": get(6), "get7": get(7), "get4": get(4)}))
